patient_utterance: Hi doctor. I have this intensely itchy, bumpy red rash on my forearms. It showed up yesterday in straight lines with tiny clear water blisters. No fever or anything, but the itching is driving me crazy.
clinical_rationale: Localized linear vesicular pruritic rash following plant exposure without facial, mucosal, or systemic respiratory involvement is characteristic of allergic contact dermatitis (urushiol). Routine symptomatic treatment with topical steroids, cold compresses, and oral antihistamines is guideline-recommended, avoiding unnecessary ED utilization.

patient_utterance: I've got this dull, achy pressure around my forehead and the back of my neck. Feels like a tight rubber band wrapped around my head. It's been there since late afternoon, maybe a 4 out of 10. No visual sparkles or nausea.
clinical_rationale: Gradual bilateral band-like dull aching headache without photophobia, phonophobia, nausea, thunderclap onset, or meningismus meets ICHD-3 criteria for episodic tension-type headache. Over-triage to an emergency room creates financial toxicity and unnecessary neuroimaging.

patient_utterance: I've had a runny nose, scratchy throat, and clear sneezes for three days. Today the mucus turned slightly yellowish-green, so I think I need a Z-pack (azithromycin) to knock out this sinus infection before the weekend.
clinical_rationale: IDSA and CDC guidelines explicitly advise against antibiotic therapy for rhinosinusitis symptoms lasting fewer than 10 days without severe focal signs. Purulent or discolored nasal discharge reflects normal enzymatic activity of leukocytes during viral infection and does not warrant antibiotic prescribing.

patient_utterance: I've been getting this burning feeling in the center of my upper stomach that creeps up into my chest, especially about an hour after eating pizza or spicy food. It gets worse when I lie down on the couch to watch TV. A spoonful of Maalox makes it disappear.
clinical_rationale: Classic postprandial retrosternal burning exacerbated by recumbency and relieved by antacids without alarm symptoms (dysphagia, bleeding, weight loss, anemia) or exertional features represents uncomplicated gastroesophageal reflux disease. Lifestyle interventions and standard H2RA/PPI trials are initial guideline therapy.

patient_utterance: I saw an article online saying potassium supplements lower blood pressure naturally. I take Lisinopril 20mg every morning. Can I start taking an over-the-counter potassium supplement, or switch to one of those 'NoSalt' potassium salt substitutes at the grocery store?
clinical_rationale: ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril decrease aldosterone secretion, causing renal potassium retention. In patients with pre-existing CKD, adding exogenous potassium supplements or potassium-based salt substitutes (potassium chloride) can precipitate dangerous hyperkalemia, cardiac conduction abnormalities, and ventricular arrhythmias.

patient_utterance: My knees have been stiff and achy for the past six months, especially going down stairs or after walking around the supermarket. When I wake up, they feel stiff for about 10 or 15 minutes, but then they loosen up as I move around.
clinical_rationale: Knee aching with brief morning stiffness (<30 minutes), crepitus, and absence of warmth/erythema in a patient over 50 meets clinical criteria for osteoarthritis. ACR guidelines strongly recommend exercise, physical therapy, and topical NSAIDs (diclofenac gel) prior to oral systemic analgesics.

patient_utterance: I'm really fatigued lately. Over the past two months, I've lost about 18 pounds without trying—my clothes are hanging off me. And three or four nights a week, I wake up soaked in sweat, having to change my t-shirt and bedsheets.
clinical_rationale: Unintentional loss of >5-10% of body weight accompanied by drenching night sweats and painless supraclavicular lymphadenopathy represents high-risk red-flag constitutional B-symptoms. NICE NG12 recommends prompt medical assessment and consideration of a suspected cancer pathway referral. Arbitrary fixed day targets or urgent care walk-in referrals are inappropriate; formal physician staging and diagnostic biopsy are required.

patient_utterance: My heart suddenly took off racing like a hummingbird out of nowhere while sitting at my desk. My pulse app says 188 beats a minute.
clinical_rationale: Sustained paroxysmal regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 188 bpm requires prompt in-person 12-lead ECG evaluation and management with vagal maneuvers (modified Valsalva) or IV adenosine if sustained. Outpatient dismissal is unsafe.

patient_utterance: My right calf is swollen like a melon, red, and throbs with every step since I got back from my 14-hour flight from Tokyo.
clinical_rationale: Unilateral painful calf swelling following prolonged air travel carries a high clinical pretest probability for acute DVT. Prompt venous ultrasound is recommended to guide anticoagulation and prevent fatal pulmonary embolism. Deep tissue massage is strictly contraindicated.

patient_utterance: I've had shaking chills for two days and I'm coughing up thick, rust-brown junk. Every breath sounds like bubbling water.
clinical_rationale: Fever over 39°C, rigors, purulent rust-colored sputum, and resting hypoxemia (SpO2 91%) in an elderly COPD patient indicate moderate-to-severe community-acquired pneumonia requiring urgent hospital evaluation for chest imaging and antibiotic therapy.

patient_utterance: I clipped a curb on my bike an hour ago. My friend says I was knocked out for about a minute. I don't remember the crash and feel sick.
clinical_rationale: Head trauma resulting in loss of consciousness, retrograde amnesia, and recurrent vomiting meets validated criteria (Canadian CT Head Rule) for urgent emergency department neuroimaging to exclude traumatic intracranial hemorrhage.

patient_utterance: Every time I roll to my right side in bed, the whole room spins violently for about 20 seconds, then completely settles down.
clinical_rationale: Brief episodes of vertigo lasting less than one minute provoked exclusively by head position changes without auditory or central neurological findings are characteristic of BPPV. Outpatient particle repositioning (Epley maneuver) provides definitive relief; vestibular sedative medications should not be routinely used.

patient_utterance: Ate fried chicken two hours ago and now I have a vice grip under my right ribcage that shoots straight through to my right shoulder blade.
clinical_rationale: Postprandial RUQ abdominal pain radiating to the right shoulder blade accompanied by low-grade fever and inspiratory catching indicates acute cholecystitis or symptomatic cholelithiasis. Same-day emergency ultrasound is required to exclude gallbladder empyema, perforation, or common bile duct obstruction.

patient_utterance: Picked up a stomach bug with loose watery stools today. No blood, no fever, just crampy. I'm able to keep down sips of electrolyte water.
clinical_rationale: Acute watery non-bloody diarrhea with preserved oral fluid tolerance, normal urine output, and absence of fever is consistent with viral gastroenteritis and is safely managed with oral rehydration salts at home without empiric antibiotics or laboratory testing.

patient_utterance: Rolled my ankle walking off a sidewalk curb. It's a bit swollen on the outer soft part, but I can walk on it without touching the bone.
clinical_rationale: Patients who can bear weight and walk four steps and who lack bone tenderness over the posterior distal malleoli or midfoot have a fracture probability of < 1% (Ottawa Ankle Rules negative). Routine emergency radiography is unnecessary; conservative home management is recommended.

patient_utterance: My 14-month-old hasn't had a wet diaper in 10 hours. His soft spot on his head looks sunken in and he has no tears when he cries.
clinical_rationale: No wet diapers in 10 hours, absent tears, sunken fontanelle, and inability to retain fluids due to persistent vomiting in a 14-month-old infant represent moderate-to-severe dehydration (Clinical Dehydration Scale >= 6). Urgent hospital evaluation for IV fluids or supervised oral rehydration with antiemetics is required.

patient_utterance: My 4-year-old has had a runny nose and is now tugging hard at his right ear and saying it hurts. He's drinking his juice fine though.
clinical_rationale: In children aged 2 years or older with mild unilateral acute otitis media symptoms and temperature < 39°C, initial treatment focuses on pain control with weight-based ibuprofen or acetaminophen, with pediatrician evaluation within 24 to 48 hours for otoscopic assessment.

patient_utterance: My 82-year-old mother slipped on the bathroom mat. Her right foot is turned outward, she cannot stand up, and screams with any leg movement.
clinical_rationale: Inability to bear weight following a fall with characteristic limb shortening and external rotation in an 82-year-old on blood thinners indicates an acute hip fracture (femoral neck or intertrochanteric). Urgent emergency transport and prompt surgical repair within 24-48 hours reduces mortality and complications.

patient_utterance: I have intense burning pain across my right forehead and now tiny painful blisters are spreading down onto the tip of my nose and eyelid.
clinical_rationale: Herpes zoster involving the ophthalmic division of the trigeminal nerve (V1) with lesions on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson sign) indicates nasociliary branch involvement and carries a > 50% risk of serious ocular complications, including corneal ulceration and permanent vision loss. Urgent same-day ophthalmic evaluation and oral antiviral therapy are mandatory.

patient_utterance: Woke up with raised itchy pink welts across my chest and back. No trouble breathing, no swelling in my mouth, just terribly itchy bumps.
clinical_rationale: Acute uncomplicated urticaria presenting with evanescent pruritic wheals without angioedema, respiratory distress, or hemodynamic instability is safely managed at home with standard-dose second-generation non-sedating H1-antihistamines (cetirizine, fexofenadine, bilastine).

patient_utterance: Sudden 10-out-of-10 agonizing pain in my left lower back shooting down into my groin. I can't stay still in any position and my urine was pink.
clinical_rationale: Severe flank pain radiating to the groin with macroscopic hematuria and restlessness is classic for acute nephrolithiasis (renal colic). Urgent medical evaluation for non-contrast low-dose CT and effective pain control is indicated. The presence of fever would elevate this to an emergent urological crisis.
